LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 13.3.1 WORD CLASSES: COMPOUND SENTENCES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.3: Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: when 1. Why do we join sentences? 2. How do we join sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify compound sentences from texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. construct compound sentences using different coordinating conjunctions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the usage of compound sentences in communication. • Read a text on the need for consumer protection and identify the compound sentences, Learners who may not turn pages to use page turners or be supported by peers. • Search online and offline for coordinating conjunctions to be used in constructing compound sentences, for example, but, or, and, so, Adjust light intensity when 1. Why do we join sentences? 2. How do we join sentences? 118 using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. • Construct compound sentences on a variety of issues including consumer protection using different conjunctions, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to construct the sentences. • Join different independent clauses using a drag and drop application or a completion table, in groups, • Display their sentences in class for peer review.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Classes: Compound Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication is enhanced as the learner communicates ideas clearly when using compound sentences.

• Digital literacy is fostered as the learner manipulates the drag and drop application.

Values:
Social justice is fostered as the learner provides support to peers through peer review.

(PCIs)

• Consumer protection is enhanced as the learner reads texts and constructs sentences on the theme.

• Effective Communication is exhibited as the learner uses compound sentence to combine ideas.
